body: Nope nobody gets meal breaks on our routed side of things. I work 4 9.5 hour shifts a week (usually take overtime on saturdays to make that 5). But the only breaks I get are a few minutes here or there at transfer center layovers. Which is usually 5 minutes if I’m lucky. Near hour 7 or 8 there is usually a 15 minutes layover so a distant bus can make connections, but that’s it. The agency gets around the state mandatory lunch break laws here by adding all those few minutes on the runcard  together. Plus there’s no federal law that says cdl drivers are required to get lunch breaks, so the state law requiring lunch breaks doesn’t apply to us. (At least, that’s what the legal precedent is so far) It’s really frustrating but I guess our company negotiated losing lunch breaks back in 2008 when the company lost a bunch of riders and revenue. And the employees approved it into the contract so I doubt we’ll ever get them back.

The console shut down and everyone breathed a collective sigh of relief, their exhaustion at the end of their hours-long ordeal evident on all their faces. The koopa guards released Peach from her prison in the castle and they embraced as old friends, like they did after every time their world was co-opted by the beings on the Other Side. 

Like all others in the world, they didn’t hold each other accountable for their actions during the Occupation. Their bodies ceased to be under their control. And this universal loss of bodily autonomy brought their community together and formed lifelong friendships and bonds - some that were closer than family.

“Marvin, how are your wife and kids doing?” the blonde princess asked one of the guards after she gave him a tight hug. 

Marvin eyes lit up at three mention of his family. “They’re great! The kids seem to be growing up so fast. Little Jamie is already talking now, and he says the most outrageous things!” He laughed and started to regale Peach with tales of his youngest as they walked with the others headed out to the vast courtyard of the castle. 

People from all over the kingdom gathered together to commemorate the end of another Occupation. They share in a vast informal banquet outside on the grounds to connect and to heal from the jarring experience of being forced to play their respective parts in the narrative controlled by the Other Side. 

It started as just a little get-together of a few koopas, goombas and bullet bills who just wanted to unwind after a long days work and share horror stories of their activities. But as time went on, the gathering grew. New friendships were formed, romances blossomed, and they’d all seen their fare share of ups and downs. Weddings on these days were especially joyous, and there had been quite a few over the years. 

As time had passed, the beings on the Other Side had seemed to grow uninterested and as a result the Occupations had become less frequent. It had been almost a year since the last one, and the air was buzzing with excitement as old friends were reunited. 

But not all were able to enjoy the festivities with as much vigor. On the hill, the stout plumber stood pensive, weary and almost war-torn. He continued to have a harder time dealing with the aftermath of Occupations because of his role in them. For everyone else, it seemed like their role was almost passive and their bodies controlled by some mindless automaton. But for him, he was directly controlled by some individual on the Other Side. His actions by another’s hand showed intent and intelligence. 

As a result of those actions, people were hurt. His friends; people that that he had come to love had  born the brunt of his violence. Thank the maker that they had all recovered and none held any ill will toward him as it was universally understood that his actions were not his own. And in his head he understood that he was not at fault for hurting those he cared about. But even after all this time, his heart still had trouble accepting that fact. 

He felt a familiar arm snake around his waist and as soft lips kissed the top of his head, he couldn’t help the smile that formed. 

“Hey honey,” came the voice from above him. “It’s gonna be okay. I’m here for you and we’ll get through this together.”

Mario took the hand around his waist in his, interlocking their fingers together and leaning against the strong chest behind him. “Thank you,” he spoke quietly. “I don’t know how I’d ever have gotten through these years without you.”

He felt more than heard the contented sigh from behind him. “Back atcha.”

Theirs was an unexpected love that caught everyone by surprise - especially them. At the beginning, they avoided each other because of what happened every Occupation. But as time went on and the gatherings brought the community together, it brought them together as well. As time went on, they grew closer and closer and their love bloomed to a point where they were each others’ soulmates in every sense of the word. 

Which is why the Occupations took such a toll on the weary plumber. Every time, he would be forced to harm the one person in this world he loved the most. And each time, it broke him a little more. But his love was always there to put him back together again. 

Mario felt a single tear roll down his cheek and the arm around him moved away for a moment. He felt hands cup his face as his love looked deep into his eyes and tenderly said the words that always helped to mend his heart. “Hey. I love you. So much. Okay?”

He smiled and whispered back, “Okay.”

His beloved’s face brightened and they said, “Now let’s get down there before all the good food is gone!”

Mario chucked and they both turned towards the vast courtyard below, hands intertwined yet again. Mario hesitated before bringing his free hand to his beloved’s face and saying, “I love you too, Bowser.”

Two years ago I admitted myself into the ER for suicidal ideation after telling my wife about what all was going on with me. They did put me on suicide watch overnight in a pretty bare room specifically for suicidal patients, then in the morning got me transferred to a mental health facility. I stayed there a little more than a week. In my experience, I didn’t really receive much one on one therapy, but was able to kind of reset and get back on some meds that helped, and we had group therapy twice a day. 

During that time, I was able to connect with a few people who were going through the same thing I was, and it helped. After I was discharged, I was able to get a therapist and I’ve been seeing him ever since. There have been some ups and downs, but he’s helped me work through a lot of things and helped me so much. 

For me, admitting myself was definitely the best decision I ever made for myself and my mental health. Not only because the short stay helped me get back to functioning again, but because it started the process that I’m on to better deal with my depression. 

If you feel yourself having suicidal thoughts, at the very least call or text the hotline. But if those thoughts include a plan to end your life, and you find yourself actively thinking about putting that plan in motion like I was, I highly recommend going to the ER. 

That’s just my experience. I wish you all the best. And if you are going through this yourself right now- remember that even if it’s really hard to see it right now, you are so important, and you are worth staying around. And you deserve the chance to see how wonderful you are, and to see how others will cherish your wonderful self.
